issue: When a sentencing enhancement turns on an offense involving child pornography under 18 U.S.C. § 2252, should the statute's listed actus reus terms be read by their ordinary, generic meaning or by reference to the federal statutory definitions?

sides.position: Statutory terms in § 2252 should be defined by reference to the federal statutory definition of 'child pornography' in the same chapter.
cases: United States v. Reinhart, 893 F.3d 606 (8th Cir. 2018)

sides.position: Terms in § 2252 should be given their ordinary, contemporary, and common meaning, not defined strictly by federal counterparts.
cases: United States v. Sullivan, 797 F.3d 623 (9th Cir. 2015)
United States v. Portanova, 961 F.3d 252 (3d Cir. 2020)

this_court: The offense should be read generically, as commonly understood and informed by its constituent terms, but not strictly cabined by them as under the formal categorical approach.
quote: As we explain in Section II.A.2, infra, other circuits have split on the appropriate treatment of individual terms in § 2252.
cite: United States v. Michael Portanova, 961 F.3d 252 (3rd Cir. 2020)
